notes: X 'views' are post impressions (how often the post was shown), not video plays, so they aren't directly comparable to other platforms.

Facebook views are exact background counts from each reel page (video_view_count). They are usually about half of the rounded 'views' Facebook displays on the Reels grid; the displayed figure is kept in the tracker as alt_views. Facebook 'likes' are reactions (rounded once over 1,000); comments aren't collected.
YouTube likes and comments aren't public without an API key, so only YouTube views are shown. YouTube Shorts view counts are rounded by YouTube (e.g. 1,300 for 1.3K).
Instagram can't be listed without logging in; only one manually listed reel is tracked (likes and comments only, no views). Instagram is mostly missing.
X history only reaches back about 7-9 months (the free API stops paging), and how far it reaches varies from run to run; older X posts keep their last collected numbers.
Cross-platform totals add different kinds of numbers (plays, impressions, background counts), so treat them as a rough reach indicator. Episodes are matched across platforms by normalized title.
Times are America/Edmonton. Each snapshot is one collection run; totals over time use the latest known numbers for each video as of that run.
